chapters.title: Getting Started
chapters.blurb: Understanding programming, Python fundamentals, and leaving garden notes.
Discover what code is, meet Python, and learn how to leave notes.

lessons.title: What is programming
lessons.lesson_content: Programming is simply giving exact, step-by-step instructions to a computer. Just like a gardening recipe, the computer follows your commands in order to bring your digital garden to life.
goals: Understand that computers follow exact step-by-step instructions
Print "Step 1: Plant seed" to give your first instruction
lessons.starter_code:
# Programming is giving exact instructions to a computer
# Print "Step 1: Plant seed" below

rules.hint: Use print("Step 1: Plant seed") to instruct the computer.

lessons.title: What is Python
lessons.lesson_content: Python is a popular, friendly programming language designed with clean syntax that reads almost like plain English. It's powerful, easy to learn, and perfect for building interactive games.
goals: Recognize Python as a friendly, readable programming language
Print "Python is ready!" to prepare your garden workspace
lessons.starter_code:
# Python reads just like plain English!
# Print "Python is ready!" below

rules.hint: Type print("Python is ready!") and click Check.

lessons.title: Leaving garden notes
lessons.lesson_content: Text after the # symbol is ignored by Python. Use comments to leave personal notes for yourself, explain your logic, or temporarily disable lines of code without deleting them.
goals: Write a comment starting with #
Print "Notes are free" so only the message runs
lessons.starter_code:
Add a # in front of this note so Python ignores it
print("Notes are free")

rules.hint: Put # at the very start of line 1: # Add a # in front...

chapters.title: First sprouts
chapters.blurb: Print, variables, data types, and basic garden math.

lessons.title: What is Programming?
lessons.lesson_content: To make your garden talk back, you use the print() function. Text wrapped inside quotation marks is outputted directly onto your console screen.
goals: Understand that programs follow instructions step by step
Display your first instruction: Step 1: Plant seed
lessons.starter_code:
# Computers follow instructions step by step
print("Step 1: Plant seed")

rules.hint: Put your text inside quotes: print("Step 1: Plant seed")

lessons.title: What is Python?
lessons.lesson_content: A variable acts like a labeled box that stores information. You give it a name, an equals sign (=), and a value so you can reference it later.
goals: Learn that Python runs code from top to bottom
Make the console say: Python is ready!
lessons.starter_code:
# Python is case-sensitive! Always use lowercase print()
print("Python is ready!")

rules.hint: Remember lowercase print: print("Python is ready!")

lessons.title: Leaving Garden Notes
Label your plant
lessons.lesson_content: Strings are text values enclosed in quotes. They are used whenever you want Python to remember names, descriptions, or messages rather than raw numbers.
goals: Create a text variable named crop set to "Sunflower"
Print crop
lessons.starter_code: # Text values (strings) always go inside quotes

rules.hint: Assign the string using quotes: crop = "Sunflower"

lessons.title: Count the seeds
lessons.lesson_content: Python can perform calculations instantly. You can multiply values using the asterisk (*) operator, whether storing them in variables or printing them directly.
goals: Use the # symbol to write a comment that Python ignores
Keep the message line active to print: Notes are free
lessons.starter_code:
# Add a # in front of this note so Python ignores it
# Plant seeds carefully
print("Notes are free")

rules.hint: Lines starting with # are notes for you. Python only runs lines without #
You can put a calculation inside print: print(a * b)

chapters.title: Growing Logic
chapters.blurb: Make smart garden decisions, repeat tasks with loops, and group crops in lists.

lessons.title: Sunny or not
lessons.lesson_content: Conditional statements (if / else) let your program make choices. If a condition is true, one path runs; otherwise, the alternative path takes over.
goals: Write an if that checks sun > 5
Add an else for the other case
Print Grow! when the sun is bright
lessons.starter_code:
sun = 8
# If sun is above 5, print Grow! Otherwise print Wait

rules.hint: End the if line with a colon and indent the next line by 4 spaces.

lessons.title: Water every plant
lessons.lesson_content: Loops let you automate repetitive tasks so you don't have to write the same line of code over and over. Using range(n) counts through numbers automatically.
goals: Use a for loop with range(3)
Print Water plant 1, Water plant 2 and Water plant 3
lessons.expected_output:
Water plant 1
Water plant 2
Water plant 3

rules.hint: range(3) counts 0, 1, 2. Print i + 1 to start at 1.

lessons.title: Seed basket
lessons.lesson_content: Lists store multiple items inside a single variable using square brackets ([]). Python starts counting items from index 0 instead of 1.
goals: Create a list named basket containing "Rose", "Mint", and "Fern"
Print the second item in the list using index 1
lessons.starter_code: # Lists store multiple items inside square brackets []

rules.hint: Python starts counting at 0, so basket[1] gets the second item.

chapters.title: First Sprouts
chapters.blurb: Displaying output, variables, plant labels, and math calculations.

lessons.title: Say Hello
goals: Use print() to say hello to your garden
Make the console say exactly: Hello, garden!
lessons.starter_code:
# Say hello to your garden
print("Hello, garden!")

rules.hint: Text goes inside quotes: print("Hello, garden!")

lessons.title: Name Your Water
goals: Create a variable named water and set it to 4
Print the variable's value using print(water)
lessons.starter_code:
# Store a number in a variable, then print it
water = 4
print(water)

rules.hint: A variable stores a value: water = 4. Print it without quotes: print(water)

lessons.title: Label Your Plant
goals: Store the plant name "Sunflower" in the crop variable
Print the plant label to the console
lessons.starter_code:
# Label your plant with a text string
crop = "Sunflower"
print(crop)

rules.hint: Words go inside quotation marks: crop = "Sunflower"

lessons.title: Count the Seeds
goals: Multiply seeds by pots using *
Print the total seeds needed (18)
lessons.starter_code:
seeds = 6
pots = 3
# Multiply seeds by pots and print total
print(seeds * pots)

rules.hint: Python uses * for multiplication: print(seeds * pots)

chapters.title: Growing Logic
chapters.blurb: Making decisions with conditionals, repeating with loops, and organizing lists.

lessons.title: Sunny or Not?
goals: Write an if that checks if sun > 5
Add an else block for when sunlight is low
Print Grow! when the sun is bright

rules.hint: End the if and else lines with a colon (:) and indent the print lines by 4 spaces.

lessons.title: Water Every Plant
goals: Use a for loop with range(3)
Print Water plant 1, Water plant 2, and Water plant 3
lessons.expected_output:
Water plant 1
Water plant 2
Water plant 3

rules.hint: range(3) counts 0, 1, 2. Use i + 1 to display 1, 2, 3!

lessons.title: Seed Basket
goals: Create a list of 3 plants with square brackets [ ]
Access and print the second plant using [1]
Make the console display: Mint
lessons.starter_code:
# Store 3 garden plants in a list
basket = ["Rose", "Mint", "Fern"]
# Print the second plant (index 1)
print(basket[1])

rules.hint: Python starts counting at index 0! So basket[0] is Rose, and basket[1] is Mint.
